solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Imbecile getting university degree that's bogus

parts.note: an ass is a fool or imbecile
MEd, Master of Education, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A fool collects a degree that turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: MEd stands for Master of Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a false name or identity that is put on is described as bogus, feigned or fake.

clue.text: Agent for washers frequently seen in residence writing up

indicators.note: one piece is seen inside the other, so the first is placed within the second
in a down clue, writing a word upwards reverses its letters

parts.note: frequently means often

explanation.surface: Something about washing machines that often turns up in written reports from a hall of residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing up' turns RES into SER, which then holds OFTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric conditioner is added in washing machines to make clothes softer, so it is an agent used in washers.

clue.text: European providing rolling news

indicators.note: rolling over turns the word for providing back to front

parts.note: providing (that) means if
N is new, and news is read as two of them, N and N

explanation.surface: A European supplying a continuous news channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' reverses IF to FI; 'news' is taken as the plural of N (new), so NN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone from Finland is a Nordic citizen of a European nation.

clue.text: Ex-sportsman's depression returned during lawsuit regularly

indicators.note: one piece occurs during the other, so it sits inside it
regularly picks every other letter of the word lawsuit
returned means the word for depression is read backwards

parts.note: a sag is a dip or depression

explanation.surface: A retired athlete's low mood returns while a court case drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every second letter of lawsuit; 'returned' turns the depression word round, and 'during' sets it inside. Andre Agassi was a US tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is a retired American tennis champion, so he is a former sportsman.

clue.text: After reflecting, fixed line that is besetting new piece of poetry

indicators.note: reflecting as in a mirror reverses the letters of the word for fixed line

parts.note: an axis is a fixed line about which something turns

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: After some thought, a settled line besieges a fresh poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflecting' turns the fixed line back to front, and 'besetting' wraps 'that is' round N. A rare word: a stanza of six lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary term: a sixaine is a stanza or poem of six lines, a piece of verse.

clue.text: Doing a zigzag line in most of Shropshire pottery

indicators.note: the line goes in the shortened county name
most of means the last letter of the county name is dropped

parts.note: Salop is an old name for Shropshire, an English county
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A wavy line drawn on a piece of pottery from Shropshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is an English county, also called Salop; 'most of' cuts it to SALO, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing a slalom course means weaving between gates, a zigzag path downhill.

clue.text: Tropical fishes, as temperature drops, stress

indicators.note: the temperature letter drops down to the bottom of the word

parts.note: tangs are tropical reef fishes

explanation.surface: Reef fish suffer stress as the water temperature falls.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the T 'drops' from the top of TANGS to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: anxiety and dread, a feeling of stress and inner turmoil.

clue.text: Gear used in Cortina that negotiates steep hill?

definitions.text: Gear used in Cortina that negotiates steep hill?

parts.words: Gear used in Cortina that negotiates steep hill?
parts.note: reads like a car's gearbox, but Cortina is the ski resort and the gear is winter-sports equipment

explanation.surface: A low gear in a Ford Cortina car for climbing a steep road.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Cortina was a popular British car; Cortina d'Ampezzo is an Italian ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment: long runners strapped to boots are the gear a skier uses on snowy slopes.

clue.text: Aquatic traveller downsized workroom

indicators.note: downsized means cut down, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a scullery is a back kitchen workroom for washing up

explanation.surface: A smaller back kitchen, oddly described as a water traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downsized' drops the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower who propels a boat with oars travels on water.

clue.text: Metal barrel opening in Gatling gun

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: The metal used for the barrel opening on a Gatling gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hard heavy element used in lamp filaments, also called wolfram, is a metal.

clue.text: Place to chill? Yes and no

definitions.text: Place to chill? Yes and no

parts.words: Place to chill? Yes and no
parts.note: a spot to relax, chilling out, though it is anything but cold

explanation.surface: A riddle about somewhere both cool and not cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hot steam room is somewhere people go to relax, though it is far from cold.

clue.text: Cold-blooded thing charged, given amount of force

parts.note: a newt is an amphibian, a cold-blooded creature
on means live or charged, as of an electric circuit

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded animal given an electric charge and some force.
explanation.definitionFit: Unit of measure: the SI unit of force, so it names an amount of force.

clue.text: Bass, served with wine, missing tail of the fish

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

indicators.note: missing means the named letter is left out

parts.note: Riesling is a white wine

indicators.note: the tail is the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sea bass served with wine, lacking its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing tail of the' removes E (last letter of 'the') from RIESLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small sprat-like sea fish, often canned as sardines, is a fish.

clue.text: Broadcaster upset costume designers essentially

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for costume is turned upside down

parts.note: garb is clothing or costume

indicators.note: essentially picks the central letter of the word designers

explanation.surface: A TV presenter irritated by the costume department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GARB into BRAG; the middle of 'designers' is G.
explanation.definitionFit: Melvyn Bragg is a long-serving British radio and TV presenter.

clue.text: Storage space's back, old fuel company removing a mixed bag

indicators.note: back means the letters of the storage term are read in reverse

parts.note: ROM, read-only memory, is computer storage space, with the 's

indicators.note: removing means the following letter is taken out

parts.note: the Gas Board was the old nationalised UK gas supplier

explanation.surface: A storeroom at the back of a former gas company's offices holds odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ROMS to SMOR; 'removing a' drops A from GASBOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative: a Swedish buffet of many dishes, used for any varied assortment.

clue.text: Winner of Manx beauty contest reportedly a bombshell?

indicators.note: reportedly signals a sound-alike of the spoken title

parts.note: the winner on the Isle of Man would be Miss Isle

explanation.surface: The Isle of Man's beauty queen described as a real stunner.
explanation.walkthrough: A beauty queen is a 'bombshell'; the answer is a literal bomb, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a guided rocket carrying a warhead is a kind of bomb, hence a playful bombshell.

clue.text: Some dressing restriction by parents inhibits one

parts.note: a ban is a restriction

indicators.note: inhibits means holds in, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: dads are fathers, parents
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Parents imposing a dress code that holds one child back.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: sticking plasters are a kind of wound dressing, here some of it.

clue.text: Copper emotional about grand chap who's been deceived

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: about means surrounding the thousand

parts.note: cold describes temperament; the word needed is really unemotional, so the clue is loose here
K, a thousand, is slang for a grand

explanation.surface: A tearful policeman over a large sum, the man who was cheated on.
explanation.walkthrough: COLD properly means unemotional, the opposite of the clue's word, so this looks like a slip; the blog reads it as unemotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional term for a man whose wife has been unfaithful to him, so he was deceived.

clue.text: Idiotic adherent's fruit dropping on Lib Dem MP

indicators.note: dropping means the next word is removed from the fruit

parts.note: a lemon is a fruit
Ming is Sir Menzies Campbell, former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A foolish follower drops fruit on a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Lib Dems are Britain's Liberal Democrat party; 'Ming' was Menzies Campbell's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative: these rodents are believed to follow one another blindly off cliffs, so the word means a mindless follower.

clue.text: Parisian who succeeded with girl initially after rejecting love rat

parts.note: qui is French for who

indicators.note: rejecting turns back the word for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, hence nil

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of girl

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who won a girl after jilting his treacherous lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is the tennis zero; 'after rejecting' turns it back. 'rat' at the end is the definition, not part of the love story.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a traitor or turncoat, named after a Norwegian collaborator, is a rat.

clue.text: Very old soldier seen in retirement homes

indicators.note: in retirement means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: so means very
ol' is a casual form of old
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An elderly soldier spotted in a retirement home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in retirement' reverses SO OL GI, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: snow-block huts built by Inuit are dwellings, a kind of home.

clue.text: English coin, changing hands, becomes this foreign one

indicators.note: changing hands swaps right for left, so R becomes L

parts.note: nicker is British slang for a pound coin

explanation.surface: A British coin, changing owners, becomes a foreign coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicker is British slang for a pound; R (right) is replaced by L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the US five-cent piece is a coin from abroad.

clue.text: Cath's outside branch entrance

indicators.note: outside takes just the outer letters of the name

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river or an organisation

explanation.surface: Cath stands outside the entrance of a local branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb, to enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enchant or captivate someone, with entrance stressed on its second syllable.

clue.text: Seafarers in midst of bankrupt state

indicators.note: the midst is the central pair of letters of bankrupt

parts.note: ILL is the abbreviation for Illinois, a US state

explanation.surface: Sailors caught up in a ruined country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' is the US state Illinois, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful: tiny shrimp-like crustaceans live in the ocean, so they are sea travellers.

clue.text: Serve woman after getting attention in pub

indicators.note: after means the woman's title follows the rest
the attention piece goes in the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to give an ear is to pay attention
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman serving drinks after catching someone's ear in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to carry weapons as a soldier is to serve in the forces.

clue.text: "Love x" seals first two letters

indicators.note: seals means closes around, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: x as in 3 x 4 is read as by
the first two letters of the alphabet are A and B

explanation.surface: A note signed with love and a kiss, sealed in an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: The x is read as the multiplication sign, 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Term of endearment: darling or sweetheart, used to address a loved one.

clue.text: Father, lingering outside earlier, heads mass frozen

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Dad, having waited outside earlier, sets off to a frozen church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a floating sheet of ice is a mass of frozen sea water.

clue.text: Judge's male friends visiting Gulf State

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so these pieces sit inside the country

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Persian Gulf
buds is US slang for friends

explanation.surface: A judge's men friends on a trip to the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: Role: an official who investigates complaints adjudicates disputes, acting as a judge.
